# Draft PR

> Opens a draft pull request for a closed task of a Gradatim project: a description, and an explainer page when the change is large. Use when the user asks for Gradatim's draft PR step, or to open, draft or create a pull request for finished work.

| | |
|---|---|
| Skill | `draft-pr`, [its file](../../skills/draft-pr/SKILL.md) |
| Step | 10 of 14: draft PR |
| Runs | After a task's close, where a pull request is due |
| Next | design task for the next task; close sprint when no task is left to do |
| Call it | `/gradatim:draft-pr` on Claude Code; [the other hosts](install.md#calling-a-skill) |

## When to use it

- The user asks for Gradatim's draft PR step, or to open, draft or create a pull request for a closed task's work.
- Not for a task that isn't closed: that is [`close-task`](close-task.md), or [`build-task`](build-task.md) where it isn't built. Not for a review of the code: that is [`close-task`](close-task.md). Not for merging the pull request, which is the user's, nor for shipping: that is [`ship-release`](ship-release.md). Not for the sprint's close: that is [`close-sprint`](close-sprint.md). Not for recording a demo: that is [`record-demo`](record-demo.md), which this step offers for a change a user sees. Not for a folder with no Gradatim project: that is [`init-project`](init-project.md).

## What it reads and writes

| Document | Path | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Agent file | `AGENTS.md` | reads |
| Agent docs | `docs/agents/<topic>.md` | reads |
| Architecture | `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | reads |
| Sprint rules and index | `docs/sprints/README.md` | reads |
| Sprint README | `docs/sprints/sprint-<n>/README.md` | reads, changes |
| Task file | `docs/sprints/sprint-<n>/<ID>-<slug>.md` | reads |
| Design | `docs/plans/<ID>-<slug>-design.md` | reads |
| PR explainer | `docs/artifacts/NN-pr-<topic>.html` | creates, changes |
| Demo walkthrough | `docs/demos/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>.mjs` | reads |
| Demo | `docs/demos/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>.webm` | reads |

It also reads the task's commits and their diff, and the project's own pull request template, where it has one. The explainer is a file in the project only where the host can't publish it, or a rule of the user's bars that. It writes none of the project's own files, and no `CLAUDE.md`.

<!-- end of the generated block -->

## Good to know

- **The explainer is published with no question** on a host that can publish, such as Claude Code. Only you see the page until you open it and share it, and the project keeps no file of it. A rule of yours against publishing keeps it in the project, in `docs/artifacts/`.
- **A rule of yours that bars git writes** leaves the push and the draft to you: the step gives each command, the title and the description, and asks for the pull request's link.
- **For a change a user sees,** with no demo on the branch yet, it asks first whether to open the draft now or to record a demo with `record-demo`.
- **Its row in the sprint's log** rides with the next step's commit, so that the pull request's checks don't run a second time.
